title: How to Prepare Your Yard for Artificial Grass Installation in Edmonton
html:
At Buksh Landscapes, we regularly encounter new clients who are eager to upgrade their backyards, but end up confused on how they can get ready to get their backyards before the actual process starts. One of the most vital methods in making your new lawn appear natural, drain well, and last several years is proper preparation.

When thinking of artificial grass installation Edmonton, we will give you a guide to help you to know all the facts about making your yard for a successful and painless project.

Why Yard Preparation Matters

It is a common belief that artificial grass just requires laying of turf on existing grass. In practice, any artificial turf installation Edmonton is highly dependent on what is under the surface.

Proper preparation helps:

  • Create a level and stable foundation
  • Improve drainage
  • Prevent weed growth
  • Extend the lifespan of the turf
  • Maintain a natural-looking appearance
  • Reduce future maintenance requirements

When done correctly, your artificial lawn can remain beautiful and functional for 15 to 20 years or more.

Step 1: Evaluate Your Existing Yard

The state of your yard should be calculated before the start of the installation.

Take note of:

  • Uneven areas
  • Low spots where water collects
  • Existing landscaping features
  • Tree roots
  • Irrigation systems
  • Drainage issues

A technical evaluation will assist in detecting the possible problems during the pre-installation stage. Because of the awareness of local soil conditions, experienced synthetic grass installers Edmonton are able to propose the most appropriate methods of preparation to ensure long-term outcomes.

We always start by having an extensive site assessment where each installation is tailored to the specific requirements of the property at Buksh Landscapes.

Step 2: Remove Existing Grass and Vegetation

The second stage would be to clean up all existing vegetation in the area to be installed.

This includes:

  • Natural grass
  • Weeds
  • Plants
  • Roots
  • Organic debris

Burying organic matter under the turf may result in uneven settlement, inadequate drainage, and outbreak of weeds in the long run.

Removal, depending on the state of your yard, may involve:

  • Sod cutting
  • Excavation
  • Weed treatment
  • Manual clearing

This operation leaves a fresh surface to the new base layer which will accommodate the artificial turf.

Step 3: Excavate the Area

One of the most significant steps in the artificial grass installation Edmonton is excavation.

In most cases, the contractors strip several inches of soil in order to have space whereby the base materials will be used to form the turf.

The extent of the excavation level is based on:

  • Soil type
  • Intended use of the lawn
  • Drainage requirements
  • Existing ground conditions

In the case of residential applications excavation can be between 3 to 6 inches.

Proper excavation means that the end product is the grass at the right height and that the grass goes in line with other landscape elements.

Step 4: Address Drainage Concerns

The Edmonton area is exceptionally vulnerable to drainage because of snowmelt throughout the seasons and the overall amount of rainfall.

The absence of effectiveness in draining can cause the water to puddle under the turf and cause problems in the long term.

The professionals consider:

  • Natural slopes
  • Water flow patterns
  • Existing drainage systems
  • Areas prone to standing water

Solutions may include:

  • Installing drainage channels
  • Creating grading slopes
  • Adding permeable base materials

Artificial turf Edmonton products are state-of-the-art turf that lets water be filtered through, but the base must be designed to facilitate drainage.

Step 5: Install a Weed Barrier

Weds occasionally bore through the soil despite being eradicated after the existing vegetation has been removed.

A high-quality weed barrier will be installed to reduce unwanted growth under the turf.

Benefits include:

  • Reduced maintenance
  • Improved appearance
  • Long-term protection
  • Prevention of invasive weeds

A weed barrier can go a long way in helping prevent future problems, although there will not ever be 100% weeds prevention, it is possible to greatly reduce their weediness.

Step 6: Build a Strong Base Layer

It is the base layer that makes your artificial lawn.

An appropriate compact base offers:

  • Stability
  • Drainage
  • Durability
  • A smooth appearance

Common base materials include:

  • Crushed rock
  • Road crush
